recipes.name: Chesapeake Bay Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon seafood seasoning (such as Old Bay®)

steps.text: Whisk together the vegetable oil, apple cider vinegar, seafood seasoning, minced garlic, basil, lime juice, and black pepper in a bowl, and pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add the pork chops, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 4 to 6 hours, flipping periodically.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate. Remove the pork chops from the bags. Discard excess marinade.
Grill until the pork is no longer pink in the center, 5 to 7 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Chesapeake Bay Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Boneless pork chops are marinated with seafood seasoning and apple cider vinegar and grilled to perfection!

review.reviewBody: Loved these! But we love Old Bay so of course we loved these. I couldnt grill these so i baked them in the marinade @ 350 for 40 mins. I will be making these again. Thanks!

This recipe was very good. I had to improvise on the Old Bay seasoning to the best of my recalling. I only made 3 chops and despite the fact that I didn't marinate it for many hours they came out actually very good. I don't have a grill so I seared them in a cast iron grill pan and then baked them for about 10 minutes at 350F and for the last 5 minutes I broiled them. By the way, I added the marinade right after they were seared and then baked the chops with it. It was very good and the smell was as usual from vinegar based dishes except that it was not overpowering in flavor. I served it with American Italian Pasta Salad from this site and it was great pairing!

After reading many reviews, I made some changes to the recipe to better suit my family’s taste. I used 3 tablespoons of the vinegar, added 3 tablespoons of chicken broth, 4 tablespoons of oil( 1/2 cup seemed a little too much for me), decreased lime juice to approximately 1/2 teaspoon and a splash of white wine to the marinade. I used a tablespoon and a half of the Old Bay Seasoning and could of used a little more. My husband and son loved the recipe and I will definitely make again. I baked the pork chops @350 degrees for 30 min and increase heat to 425 for about 10 minutes more.

Yummy! Also took the leftovers the next day and any juice left on them, cut them up mixed with diced tomatoes, finely chopped shallots, a little more Old Bay and a little fresh cilantro and heated it up in microwave. Ate it with some of that 90 second rice and it was yummy for the second day! Can't wait to have it again - and make extra for leftovers!

This was excellent. I had to make my own seafood seasoning using another recipe, but the vinegar was the perfect amount for me (for what it's worth, I LOVE salt & vinegar potato chips, so I'm a fan of that taste!). I marinated the pork chops about 4.5 hours, and the acid actually cooked them a tiny bit. I grilled them on the George Foreman, and while they didn't get the nice char marks from an outdoor grill, they came out perfectly anyway. Juicy, and very flavorful. Easy to make. I will again. I served them with mashed potatoes.

We loved this recipe. I only marinated about 20 minutes. I cooked it in the marinade in the oven. Turned out great. I didn’t use all the vinegar but I will next time and I used more Old Bay seasoning. I will be making this again!!

My family and I liked this dish a lot. I halved the vinegar as other recommended and am glad I did. Also used lemon instead of lime and baked it for 40 minutes at 350. We love Old Bay, so I did sprinkle some on top of the chops before baking. Will certainly make this again and recommended it to a neighbor!

The first thing I want to mention is this recipe does not do as well with pork loin chops- loin is simply too dry a cut to not have a marinade to break down the fibers. You would be well advised to get a slightly fattier cut of chop to make it tastier. The marinade is very light and should be used the maximum amount of time possible. I read some people's opinion regarding the Old Bay being overpowering but I don't know how that could be with this recipe, even if you added slightly more. I was unable to taste the Old Bay in the marinade but it was fine once lightly sprinkled on the chops. Don't do this until the chops are warming as opposed to cooking, you don't want to burn the spices. I think this was a more unusual recipe, simple, and I will be trying it again with those few changes.

Terrific marinade! After reading reviews I made the following changes to suit our tastes... Cut the apple cider vinegar in half, add 1/4 cup of water and double the Old Bay Seasoning. Sprinkle with Old Bay Seasoning before broiling on my George Foreman! The chops were tender and delicious. I will try this on chicken very soon, adding a tbsp of Soy Sauce!

so very tender and moist - as other reviewers recommended, halved (white balsamic, cuz that's what I had) vinegar and oil, doubled Old Bay, used lemon juice (didn't have a lime) & teaspoon of dried basil (no fresh right now) and then baked in the marinade...and so easy!

My husband gave this four stars. It was very moist and tasty. I grilled 2 chops, so I adjusted the measurements but used too much apple cider vinegar. (My husband is not a vinegar fan.) I seared on an indoor griddle then finished in a 325 convection oven for about 6 minutes. I will make this again!

cut down the vinegar but was still a bit strong. pork in oven turned out a bit tough even cutting down the cooking time on the low end due to relatively thin boneless pork chop, ie 15 min at 350deg. Will try again and reduce time further checking temp frequently.
We liked these pork chops. They had a nice subtle flavor and didn't overpower the pork flavor. Will make these again.

I didnt have a fresh lime, so Alexa guided me to a 2 tablespoon equivalent. That is the only change i made. The dominant taste of the meat was "sour". Overwhelming vinegar taste. My wife, who is not fussy, wouldnt eat it. She said it was also dry, tough, and she couldnt get past the vinegar either. I expected more of an Old Bay flavor, but barely noticed it. This is also my first negative review of a recipe here.
Made according to recipe. Excellent flavor, moist and will make again.
Made these pork chops a few times now followed instructions and they’ve turned out great every time.

Our chops turned out moist and juicy but, alas, not much of the Old Bay flavor. I marinated the chops 6 hours then, following the advice of other writers, I also sprinkled more Old Bay on the chops on the grill. Next time, I'll increase the Old Bay in both the marinade and on the grill. Neither my wife nor I detected any objectionable smell or taste from the apple cider vinegar - in fact, we thought it was quite faint. We were expecting more based on the numerous comments. Other than grilling longer to allow for our 1 1/2 inch thick chops, we followed the recipe. This is a good-not-great marinade. I hope that increasing the Old Bay will noticeably improve it.
Good recipe! I love Old Bay seasoning so I think I might add to the amount next time.
To much vinegar for me. I would double the old bay and half the vinegar next time.
